newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee to move sideways, must break range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee to move sideways, must break range.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures should move sideways for the time being, but will run into upside pressure while trying to break out of recent stifling ranges, technical analysts said on Thursday.
Traders called the market to open unchanged to slightly lower than Wednesday's close.
Although London closed firmer and at session highs on Wednesday, dealings were thin throughout -- mainly as a result of Friday's U.S. Independence Day holiday.

Technical analysts said the London market seemed content to continue its tight sideways movements for the time being and was unlikely to see any major breakout in the absence of the New York market on Friday.
"We're still in that range and, if anything, the range is getting a bit narrower now," said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden.
But there was also a certain amount of technical pressure to the upside which might act as a slight barrier to attempts at a rally, he said.
September's shorter-term moving averages were either within the current trading range -- a mere $24 during Wednesday's session -- or above the market.

"That might have an effect in the longer run but I think short-term sideways until we see a breakout," Haylor said, pegging nearby support at $1,750 and initial resistance at $1,889 but extending up to $2,000.
In fundamental news, independent weather forecaster WSC said there was no damaging cold in sight for the next seven days in Brazil's coffee areas.
Temperatures were expected to be near normal to slightly above normal in the next few days with cooler weather forecast for Sunday.
